requirements.statement: The specification system **MUST** preserve Figma-class authoring and PowerPoint-class production and delivery as equal constitutional pillars.
Every normative concept **MUST** have exactly one numbered owner at an accepted revision.
The authority resolver **MUST** use the precedence order defined in Section 3.1 for active conflicts.
A lower-authority artifact **MUST NOT** narrow an accepted parent capability without an adopted decision by its numbered owner.
A numbered volume **MUST** declare its normative scope, explicit non-ownership, supersession, owner, maturity, and version metadata.
Every atomic requirement **MUST** contain exactly one primary all-capitals RFC 2119 keyword in its normative statement.
Every atomic requirement **MUST** express one independently acceptable or rejectable outcome.
Every atomic requirement **MUST** link to at least one immutable `DES-*`, `PRE-*`, or `ARC-*` parent capability.
Every allocated specification identifier **MUST** remain reserved for its original semantic outcome.
A requirement moved to a different normative volume **MUST** receive a new ID with bidirectional supersession links.
Every accepted requirement **MUST** identify its applicable surfaces and lifecycle boundaries.
Every accepted requirement **MUST** define observable failure or recovery behavior for each applicable non-happy-path state.
Every accepted requirement **MUST** link to at least one pass/fail acceptance criterion.
Every active acceptance criterion **MUST** identify every requirement it evaluates.
Traceability **MUST** remain navigable in both parent-to-child and child-to-parent directions.
Specification maturity **MUST** remain independent from delivery, verification, freshness, and release-applicability status.
A conformance claim **MUST** identify the exact product revision, specification revision, environment profile, and observation date.
A derived status or coverage view **MUST** declare its source revision and generation or review date.
Deferred, unsupported, or waived accepted scope **MUST** remain visible in traceability.
Coverage **MUST NOT** be inferred solely from filenames, labels, controls, screenshots, source symbols, or test titles.
Every behavioral specification change **MUST** follow `FLOW-00-001`.
Every conflict between accepted normative statements **MUST** follow `FLOW-00-002`.
Every accepted behavior-changing decision **MUST** record rationale, alternatives, consequences, and affected IDs in an adopted `ADR-*`.
Superseding a requirement **MUST** define migration for every affected durable or learned user contract.
An accepted open decision that can affect implementation **MUST** state a default behavior in force, owner, and review trigger.
An editorial change **MUST NOT** alter an observable outcome, default, state, threshold, permission, data meaning, or acceptance result.
Every evidence record **MUST** contain the minimum fields defined in Section 11.1.
Evidence used for conformance **MUST** observe the actual boundary claimed by the acceptance criterion.
User-observable browser evidence **MUST** be captured in a visible headed browser.
A workflow that produces a file, clipboard payload, recording, or exported artifact **MUST** include semantic artifact inspection in its acceptance evidence.
A visual conformance claim **MUST** include rendered paint or pixel evidence on the applicable real surface.
A collaboration conformance claim **MUST** include independent-client operation and convergence evidence.
Every conformance suite **MUST** include at least one discriminating negative case for each material product claim.
Rerunning a protocol **MUST** create a new immutable evidence record.
A waiver **MUST** include bounded scope, rationale, mitigation, disclosure, owner, issue, expiry, retest condition, and approvals.
A release **MUST NOT** claim conformance by waiving a non-waivable condition from Section 12.2.
An accepted domain specification **MUST** pass every applicable completeness item in Section 13.2.
A deliberate difference from a benchmark convention **MUST** be documented as an accepted Story-specific exception or remain classified as a parity gap.
Canonical terminology **MUST** use one meaning across requirements, UI copy, schemas, tests, and evidence.
Every release conformance record **MUST** disclose included, failing, missing, stale, waived, and profile-excluded accepted requirements.
Story **MUST** treat Figma-class visual authoring and PowerPoint-class presentation production and delivery as equal product pillars.
Story **MUST** provide one coherent bridge from reusable visual and narrative systems to deterministic audience delivery.
The authoring presentation **MUST** remain the semantic source of truth across editor, runtime, and professional outputs.
The primary product wedge **MUST** serve design-led teams that repeatedly adapt high-stakes presentations for multiple audiences.
Product positioning **MUST NOT** claim parity from chrome resemblance, control count, or flattened visual output.
Optional automation or AI **MUST NOT** become required for deterministic core authoring, preservation, delivery, or output.
Story **MUST** let experienced visual designers transfer common object-authoring knowledge without relearning contradictory core interactions.
Story **MUST** let experienced presentation authors transfer common document and delivery knowledge without leaving Story for core workflows.
Story **MUST** give presenters deterministic readiness, private state, navigation, and recovery for high-stakes delivery.
Story **MUST** let reviewers identify the exact edition, revision, audience scope, and anchored content under review.
Story **MUST** let organizations govern shared sources and permissions without preventing attributable audience-specific adaptation.
Story **MUST** treat accessible operation and accessible presentation output as primary professional user jobs.
Comparable object-authoring interactions **MUST** follow Figma jurisdiction unless an accepted Story-specific exception demonstrates measurable benefit.
Comparable presentation-document and delivery interactions **MUST** follow PowerPoint jurisdiction unless an accepted Story-specific exception demonstrates measurable benefit.
Story-native bridge interactions **MUST** use a coherent native model for systems, narratives, editions, overrides, and runtime snapshots.
A cross-jurisdiction command collision **MUST** resolve according to the user's visible object of intent and active scope.
A deliberate jurisdictional divergence **MUST** disclose its behavior at the point of learning and in the command reference.
Story **MUST** expose a Story System as the governed relationship among reusable visual, presentation, narrative, audience, and delivery semantics.
A base narrative **MUST** preserve explicit semantic order and role independently of any one audience edition.
A narrative component **MUST** preserve semantic role, slots, states, accessibility contract, and source identity independently of visual realization.
An audience edition **MUST** represent audience-specific differences as non-destructive deltas from a base narrative.
A governed override **MUST** expose stable source, target, scope, provenance, and reconciliation state.
A runtime snapshot **MUST** bind an immutable validated document revision, edition, context, readiness result, and capability profile.
Authoring after runtime admission **MUST** create or require a new snapshot rather than mutate the admitted snapshot.
Compatible shared-source updates **MUST** preserve intentional local overrides by stable semantic identity.
Incompatible shared-source updates **MUST** produce reviewable conflict or orphan states without choosing a silent winner.
Creating an audience variation **MUST NOT** duplicate the presentation unless the user explicitly chooses an independent copy boundary.
Edition authoring **MUST** show the selected audience and material differences from the base before readiness validation.
Every irreversible interchange or destructive conversion boundary **MUST** disclose lost editability and semantic degradation before commit.
Story-native semantics **MUST** remain traceable through editor, runtime, and supported artifact surfaces.
Destructive authoring transformations **MUST** require explicit intent and one recoverable transaction before external irreversible commit.
A new capability **MUST** use the shared document and surface fidelity contract rather than create an isolated semantic path.
Interaction hot paths **MUST NOT** synchronously perform unrelated indexing, network, whole-document serialization, or equivalent heavy work.
User content **MUST NOT** leave the declared trust boundary without informed consent, purpose, minimization, and retention policy.
Private presenter state **MUST NOT** appear on the audience surface without explicit publication as authored audience content.
Accessibility semantics **MUST** remain authored, reviewable meaning across supported editor, runtime, and output surfaces.
Core local authoring **MUST** degrade predictably when authentication, network, or cloud providers are unavailable.
Product capability claims **MUST** use evidence admissible under Volume 00 for the exact boundary claimed.
Figma-class parity **MUST** cover the representative professional object-authoring workflows listed in Section 10.2.
PowerPoint-class parity **MUST** cover the representative professional document and delivery workflows listed in Section 10.3.
Every parity boundary **MUST** classify bounded or unsupported behavior without deleting it from accepted scope.
A flattened raster or screenshot **MUST NOT** satisfy an editable-authoring parity claim.
Unsupported imported source data **MUST** be preserved according to the declared fidelity tier or reported before loss.
A novel capability **MUST NOT** introduce a second authoritative document, history, rendering, file, or collaboration model.
Design-authoring knowledge transfer **MUST** meet `SLO-01-001`.
Presentation-authoring knowledge transfer **MUST** meet `SLO-01-002`.
The primary wedge workflow **MUST** meet `SLO-01-003`, `SLO-01-005`, and `SLO-01-010`.
Source, scope, and update comprehension **MUST** meet `SLO-01-004` and `SLO-01-006`.
Readiness and delivery recovery **MUST** meet `SLO-01-007` and `SLO-01-008`.
Interchange consequence comprehension **MUST** meet `SLO-01-009`.
The Authoring Workspace **MUST** use the canonical command-bar, navigator, primary-workspace, inspector, tool-dock, and optional-tray shell defined in Section 3.
A no-document session **MUST** present the task-oriented Document Hub inside the app shell rather than a marketing landing page.
The global command bar **MUST** keep document identity, durable save/provider state, context identity, and delivery entry available.
The navigator **MUST** adapt its structure to the current view and edit scope without creating a second selection model.
The primary workspace **MUST** receive the largest contiguous authoring region permitted by active accessibility and adaptive constraints.
The inspector **MUST** show properties for the current selection or edit scope with truthful source, mixed, applicability, and permission states.
Direct-manipulation views **MUST** provide one stable tool dock whose state and shortcuts match the active tool model.
Speaker notes **MUST** be available as both an optional authoring tray and a dedicated Notes view.
Canvas fit operations **MUST** use the unobscured workspace after accounting for docked rails, trays, overlays, and the tool-dock safe inset.
Shell layout preferences **MUST NOT** become authored presentation state.
Story **MUST** represent Canvas, Grid, Outline, Notes, and System as independent workspace views.
Switching views **MUST** preserve document, base/edition context, compatible edit scope, and compatible selection.
Story **MUST** represent the authored mutation owner as an edit scope independent from view and runtime mode.
A non-default edit scope **MUST** remain visibly identified before and during every allowed mutation.
Master and layout authoring **MUST** use edit-scope transitions rather than an overloaded global runtime-mode value.
Edition scope **MUST** keep audience identity, base source, and difference state visible in every compatible view.
Activating a tool **MUST** change input interpretation without mutating authored content.
A temporary tool **MUST** restore the immediately preceding compatible tool when the temporary interaction ends.
The Shape tool **MUST** use one stable split-tool slot for all registered shape kinds.
A successful creation gesture **MUST** commit exactly one object transaction and select the created object.
Preview, Rehearsal, Recording, Presentation, and Kiosk **MUST** be represented as runtime modes independent from authoring edit scopes.
Editor, Audience, Presenter, Recorder controller, and Remote controller **MUST** be represented as explicit surface roles with separate visibility policy.
Exiting runtime **MUST** restore the nearest valid captured authoring context and focus.
Comparable object-authoring shell behavior **MUST** follow Figma jurisdiction or an accepted Story-specific exception.
Comparable presentation-document and delivery shell behavior **MUST** follow PowerPoint jurisdiction or an accepted Story-specific exception.
Story Systems, narratives, editions, governed overrides, and runtime snapshots **MUST** use the Story-native interaction model in this volume.
Canvas, Layers, Grid, and navigator surfaces **MUST** synchronize selections when they address the same entities.
Multi-selection controls **MUST** implement the uniform, mixed, unset, and not-applicable model in Section 9.4.
A relative multi-selection edit **MUST** preserve each target's gesture-start difference.
Every menu, shortcut, toolbar, context-menu, and inspector invocation of an action **MUST** route through one canonical command identity.
A displayed shortcut **MUST** invoke its labeled command in the displayed context.
Shortcut routing **MUST** follow the context priority in Section 10.3.
Story **MUST NOT** intercept the critical browser and operating-system shortcuts reserved in Section 10.4.
The Authoring Workspace **MUST** expose the ordered primary focus regions and F6 navigation defined in Section 11.1.
Closing a transient surface **MUST** restore focus to its valid invoker or nearest valid region.
A modal dialog **MUST** trap focus and make background regions inert until resolution.
One Escape key event **MUST** unwind exactly one highest-priority applicable level from Section 12.2.
Canceling an active preview **MUST** restore the complete gesture-start authored and selection state.
Escape in a draft inspector or inline-rename control **MUST** restore the focus-entry value without changing the broader selection.
Escape from canvas rich-text editing **MUST** preserve accepted text operations while canceling only active composition and leaving one edit depth.
Enter, Tab, and blur **MUST** follow the control-specific valid-commit policy in Section 12.3.
A continuous interaction **MUST** produce at most one committed authored transaction.
A feature workflow **MUST** use the smallest surface type that preserves its required context and decisions under Section 13.2.
An inspector popover **MUST** remain bounded to one property or tightly coupled property group.
A navigable, comparative, or multi-step system workflow **MUST** use a dedicated full view rather than nested panels or dialogs.
A window **MUST** maintain at most one active unrelated transient popover chain.
Panel placement, size, collapse, scroll, and selected-tab state **MUST** remain editor-session or user-preference state.
The shell **MUST** represent every applicable document state in Section 14.1 with a visible next safe action.
Every interactive control **MUST** expose all applicable interaction, validation, permission, busy, and mixed states from Section 14.3.
An error message **MUST** identify the failed outcome, known cause, preserved state, and primary safe recovery action.
Shell adaptation **MUST** use the effective W4-W1 tiers and deterministic collapse order in Section 15.
Adaptive reflow **MUST** preserve semantic context, valid drafts, selection, and committed work.
Input density **MUST** adapt to the current interaction modality without treating all touch-capable devices as coarse-pointer sessions.
The D1 companion tier **MUST** support the bounded navigation, review, comment, notes, presentation, and emergency-correction workflows in Section 15.3.
Critical workflows **MUST** remain operable at the browser zoom and reflow conditions in Section 15.6.
Every critical workflow **MUST** provide a complete keyboard path with visible focus.
Coarse-pointer interactions **MUST** provide at least 44 by 44 CSS-pixel hit targets without relying on hover.
Focus, selection, state, source, warnings, errors, and collaborator identity **MUST** remain perceivable without color alone.
User-facing labels **MUST** use the canonical terms and command grammar in Section 17.
The shell **MUST** implement the Quiet Stagecraft spatial and craft principles in Section 18.
App themes **MUST** implement the semantic roles and geometry constraints in Section 19 without changing authored presentation semantics.
Context orientation and shell findability **MUST** meet `SLO-14-053` and `SLO-14-054`.
Command, Escape, and commit predictability **MUST** meet `SLO-14-055`, `SLO-14-056`, and `SLO-14-057`.
Property, focus, adaptive, state, language, visual-consistency, and touch outcomes **MUST** meet `SLO-14-058` through `SLO-14-064`.
A Story presentation **MUST** have exactly one valid `StoryDocument` root conforming to `SCH-03-001`.
Persisted authored state **MUST** exclude editor, identity, presence, provider, cache, decoded-resource, and playback state.
Every independently addressable authored entity and sub-entity **MUST** have a stable document-wide identifier governed by `SCH-03-002`.
Every semantically ordered collection **MUST** use the identity-preserving collection contract in `SCH-03-003`.
Every persisted spatial, angular, temporal, scalar, and color value **MUST** use the units and coordinate conventions in `SCH-03-004`.
Every cross-entity relationship **MUST** use a typed reference and the dangling-reference behavior in `SCH-03-005`.
Readers and writers **MUST** preserve unknown compatible fields and opaque entities according to `SCH-03-006`.
Each optional property **MUST** distinguish omission, empty value, explicit clear, invalid value, and unresolved reference as specified by its schema.
Document metadata and page setup **MUST** conform to `SCH-03-007` without making display names or timestamps part of identity.
Slides, sections, and custom shows **MUST** retain stable membership and independent semantic order.
Slide masters, layouts, and placeholders **MUST** use explicit ownership and inheritance references conforming to `SCH-03-008`.
Presentation themes and reusable styles **MUST** store authored tokens separately from app-theme or resolved paint values.
Variables, collections, modes, aliases, and bindings **MUST** conform to the typed acyclic contract in `SCH-03-009`.
Component definitions, component sets, variants, and component properties **MUST** conform to `SCH-03-010`.
Component instances and inherited slide content **MUST** express local differences as stable override records conforming to `SCH-03-011`.
Reusable narrative components **MUST** preserve semantic roles, slots, states, and source identity independently of their visual realization.
Audience editions **MUST** express inclusion, ordering, content substitution, and variable-mode choices as non-destructive deltas from a base narrative.
Every placed element **MUST** use one base node contract plus exactly one registered element payload kind.
Ordered fills, strokes, effects, paths, points, segments, operands, cells, series, animation steps, and other editable sub-items **MUST** retain sub-identities across reorder and value edits.
Rich text **MUST** persist content, paragraph structure, character spans, list identity, language, direction, and bindings without relying on renderer markup.
Tables, charts, diagrams, and linked data objects **MUST** preserve structured source data and stable row, cell, series, node, and relationship identities.
Media-bearing content **MUST** reference asset descriptors by durable asset identity rather than object URL, cache key, provider URL, or decoded bytes.
Object animation **MUST** persist stable targets, triggers, timing, effect parameters, and deterministic sequence membership using `SCH-03-012`.
Slide transitions **MUST** persist authored transition intent separately from runtime readiness, frame, or clock state.
Speaker notes and comment threads **MUST** persist as structured authored content with stable anchors and lifecycle state.
Reading order, alternative descriptions, decorative state, language, captions, and table-header semantics **MUST** be first-class authored properties where applicable.
Deletion **MUST** produce an addressable tombstone whenever history, collaboration, recovery, interchange, or an extant reference can still require the deleted identity.
Schema validation **MUST** return deterministic, addressable diagnostics without partially mutating the candidate document.
Every schema migration **MUST** be deterministic, idempotent, version-gated, diagnosable, and preservation-safe.
Semantically equivalent documents **MUST** produce the same canonical semantic hash under `SCH-03-015`.
Copy, paste, duplicate, import, and template instantiation **MUST** remap owned identities while preserving declared external and shared references.
Derived resolution, layout, tessellation, thumbnail, search, decode, and render-cache data **MUST NOT** be authoritative fields in the canonical document.
Every canonical document mutation **MUST** cross exactly one typed transaction boundary.
Every transaction **MUST** conform to the envelope and lifecycle contract in `SCH-04-001`.
Every operation **MUST** conform to the common typed envelope in `SCH-04-002`.
A transaction **MUST** name an immutable base revision and semantic hash before validation or application.
Interactive editing **MUST** isolate preview values from the accepted canonical document until commit.
Cancelling or abandoning a preview **MUST** restore the accepted view without emitting document operations or history.
Commit validation and operation application **MUST** be atomic across all operations in the transaction.
Operation validation **MUST** use the same canonical schemas for local commits, remote submissions, undo, redo, migration adapters, imports, and automation.
Mutation targets **MUST** use stable typed addresses and expected kinds rather than indexes, names, or renderer locations.
Property operations **MUST** encode explicit final values or explicit clear/unset semantics rather than ambiguous null or implicit deltas.
Ordered-collection operations **MUST** target stable order-entry identities and relative anchors conforming to `SCH-04-005`.
Create, duplicate, paste, instantiate, detach, and import operations **MUST** carry complete identity allocation or remapping before application.
Delete operations **MUST** declare reference policy, tombstone behavior, and sufficient inverse material before commit.
Text, vector, style-stack, table, chart, diagram, component, master/layout, notes, comment, asset-reference, and animation edits **MUST** use registered semantic operation families.
A failed precondition or operation **MUST** reject the whole transaction without exposing a partially mutated document.
A successful commit **MUST** produce a new immutable revision, post-state semantic hash, applied-operation record, and deterministic diagnostics.
Every committed user transaction **MUST** provide a semantic inverse or an explicitly bounded snapshot-backed inverse conforming to `SCH-04-009`.
Continuous pointer, pen, scrub, drawing, and text-edit sessions **MUST** coalesce into the transaction granularity defined by `SCH-04-010`.
A transaction whose canonical before and after semantic hashes are equal **MUST NOT** create accepted document history.
Replaying an admitted transaction stream from the same base **MUST** produce the same result, diagnostics, and semantic hash.
Duplicate receipt of an accepted transaction or operation ID **MUST** be idempotent and return the recorded outcome without reapplication.
Accepted revisions **MUST** form a verifiable parent/hash chain with no dependence on wall-clock ordering.
Local undo eligibility **MUST** include only the actor's accepted, undoable, non-undone intents in the current branch.
Local undo **MUST** apply a validated compensating transaction to current accepted state without removing accepted remote work.
Redo **MUST** re-express the undone intent against current accepted state and report any now-inapplicable portion.
A rejected pending local transaction **MUST** be removed from the optimistic projection and assigned one explicit rejection disposition from `SCH-04-013`.
When authority accepts a transformed transaction, the client **MUST** replace the optimistic form with the canonical accepted form and deterministically rebase later local intent.
Offline and pending transactions **MUST** retain causal dependencies, base identity, retry identity, and user-visible disposition until accepted, rejected, or explicitly discarded.
Transactions with unsatisfied causal or entity dependencies **MUST** remain buffered or reject with typed dependency diagnostics rather than apply out of order.
Permission, schema, feature, quota, and policy rejection **MUST** be distinguishable from conflict, stale-base, missing-target, and transport failure.
Migrations and deterministic repair **MUST** use typed system transactions or a versioned pure migration boundary with no user undo entry.
Mutation telemetry **MUST** expose bounded lifecycle, latency, rejection, coalescing, replay, and hash-verification hooks without authored values.
Every product surface **MUST** consume a scene produced by the canonical resolver contract in `SCH-05-001`.
Resolution **MUST** be non-mutating and deterministic for identical pinned inputs.
Resolution precedence **MUST** follow `SCH-05-002` independently of object insertion order and renderer behavior.
Every resolved property **MUST** retain its winning source, overridden sources, fallback state, and diagnostics according to `SCH-05-003`.
Inherit, explicit clear, authored empty, missing, invalid, unresolved, and unsupported states **MUST** remain distinguishable through resolution.
Theme, style, variable, mode, alias, and fallback resolution **MUST** use one typed acyclic value-resolution pipeline.
Master, layout, placeholder, slide, and edition resolution **MUST** preserve stable source identity and valid local overrides.
Component, variant, property, nested-instance, and override resolution **MUST** preserve source editability and report orphaned addresses.
Narrative and audience-edition resolution **MUST** produce an explicit ordered presentation sequence without mutating base narratives or slides.
Layout and constraint resolution **MUST** produce finite canonical geometry using declared coordinate spaces and deterministic algorithms.
The resolved scene **MUST** conform to the renderer-neutral root and node contracts in `SCH-05-005` through `SCH-05-007`.
Scene traversal and paint order **MUST** derive from semantic order and hierarchy, never from map order or adapter sorting.
Geometry, clipping, masks, booleans, and transforms **MUST** have one backend-neutral semantic representation.
Fill, stroke, effect, blend, opacity, and compositing semantics **MUST** preserve ordered layer identity and explicit color space.
Text resolution **MUST** preserve structured text, shaping inputs, layout metrics, language, direction, fallback fonts, and semantic ranges independently of renderer markup.
Tables, charts, diagrams, equations, and data-bound visuals **MUST** retain semantic structure and accessible descriptions alongside visual primitives.
Media scene nodes **MUST** declare asset identity, crop/fit, poster, timing, captions, controls policy, and fallback without embedding provider URLs.
Accessibility semantics and reading order **MUST** be part of the common scene rather than reconstructed independently by each surface.
Animation and transition evaluation **MUST** produce deterministic scene snapshots for the same authored timeline, input event sequence, and logical time.
The scene **MUST** expose a complete resource dependency and readiness plan before a time-critical surface presents it.
Resource readiness **MUST** distinguish ready, loading, missing, corrupt, blocked, unsupported, and timed-out states with feature-specific fallbacks.
Each surface adapter **MUST** declare capabilities and negotiate a `SurfacePlan` before emitting pixels or artifacts.
Surface-specific substitution, rasterization, flattening, omission, preservation-only handling, or blocking **MUST** create an addressable degradation record.
Each adapter **MUST** consume defined scene semantics instead of independently reinterpreting raw canonical document fields.
Editor, thumbnail, presentation, presenter, export, print, and recording content **MUST** be semantically equivalent after accounting for declared viewport, time, and degradation context.
Authoring affordances and presenter-private UI **MUST** be isolated from audience, export, print, and recording content scenes.
Empty scenes, hidden nodes, decorative nodes, unresolved opaque nodes, and fully clipped nodes **MUST** have explicit paint, hit-test, and accessibility behavior.
Scene and adapter caches **MUST** key on all semantic inputs, validate dependency hashes, and remain non-authoritative.
Rendering failures **MUST** be contained to the smallest addressable scene unit while preserving a coherent surface and diagnostics.
Cross-surface conformance **MUST** compare semantic captures as well as visual output for representative fixture corpora.
Render, scene, and resource hashes **MUST** be deterministic within a declared renderer/profile version and separate from the document semantic hash.
Resolution and rendering telemetry **MUST** expose bounded timing, cache, readiness, degradation, and failure hooks without authored content or asset locators.
Native Story presentations **MUST** use the `.str` extension, `application/x-story-presentation` media type, and one versioned package contract.
Every portable `.str` package **MUST** conform to the logical layout and path rules in `SCH-06-001`.
Every package **MUST** contain one valid bootstrap manifest conforming to `SCH-06-002` and pointing to one immutable head revision.
Every package revision **MUST** conform to `SCH-06-003` and bind document semantic hash, accepted document revision, parent package revision, object graph, and feature versions.
Canonical JSON and binary package objects **MUST** be content-addressed and integrity-verified according to `SCH-06-004`.
Package sharding **MUST** preserve canonical document meaning and semantic hash independently of chunk boundaries, compression, paths, or entry order.
Readers **MUST** validate container safety, manifest, feature compatibility, hashes, required objects, canonical schema, references, and semantic hash before mutable admission.
Readers **MUST** preserve compatible unknown manifest fields, indexed objects, extensions, and opaque document data across save/open.
Preview and derived-cache entries **MUST** be optional, integrity-bound, disposable, and incapable of overriding canonical document or asset objects.
A save **MUST** freeze one accepted canonical document revision and dependency closure without blocking subsequent document transactions.
Save assembly **MUST** use copy-on-write staging while leaving the only committed package untouched by append, patch, truncation, or rewrite.
A staged save candidate **MUST** be closed, reopened, and fully verified before it is eligible for publication.
Publishing a revision **MUST** use atomic replace or conditional compare-and-swap against an expected durable head/version token.
A destination lacking atomic replace and conditional publication **MUST** use a new sibling/copy or remain local-checkpoint-only while leaving the sole verified copy untouched.
A save acknowledgment **MUST** identify the committed package revision and durable destination version in a form recoverable after an ambiguous transport response.
Changes accepted after a save snapshot **MUST** remain dirty after that older snapshot is published.
Every storage provider **MUST** declare the capability and consistency profile in `SCH-06-008` before a save strategy is selected.
Cloud and external saves **MUST** detect head/version conflicts before replacement and reject unconditional last-writer-wins.
Resumable or multipart upload **MUST** preserve one save identity, expected head token, byte ranges, object hashes, and final candidate verification.
Cross-tab writers **MUST** use an atomic lease with a monotonically increasing fencing token plus a destination compare-and-swap or non-overlapping exclusive publication guard.
A stale or partitioned tab **MUST** be unable to publish after a newer fencing token or destination head has been issued.
Asset import **MUST** validate size, signature, media type, security policy, and full SHA-256 content identity before canonical registration.
Before transaction acceptance, referenced asset bytes **MUST** exist in verified durable local staging or a verified immutable remote object.
Original assets, generated variants, posters, proxies, and transcoded outputs **MUST** have distinct content identities and explicit provenance relationships.
Asset garbage collection **MUST** use verified reachability plus retention pins for live documents, revisions, inverses, pending transactions, checkpoints, uploads, and preserved unknown data.
Linked assets **MUST** retain durable locator, integrity, offline, permission, fallback, and embed/relink semantics distinct from embedded assets.
Each accepted semantic change **MUST** schedule a background local recovery checkpoint without performing unrelated storage work in the interaction hot path.
A recovery checkpoint **MUST** conform to `SCH-06-012` and preserve accepted state, eligible pending intent, staged assets, base lineage, and integrity.
Autosave status **MUST** distinguish dirty, locally checkpointed, externally publishing, externally saved, conflict, blocked, and failed states.
Autosave and manual save **MUST** serialize through one save coordinator while allowing newer snapshots to queue without mutating an in-flight candidate.
Startup and reopen **MUST** discover and independently verify committed heads, local checkpoints, interrupted-save journals, provider versions, and conflict copies before recovery choice.
Recovery **MUST** automatically choose a candidate only when ancestry and operation coverage prove it cannot discard accepted or eligible pending intent.
Divergent valid recovery candidates **MUST** remain preserved and require operation-level merge, explicit branch choice, or conflict-copy creation.
Corrupt, partial, newer-version, unknown-required-feature, missing-asset, permission, quota, offline, and canceled paths **MUST** have distinct non-destructive outcomes.
Migration **MUST** retain the original revision and commit migrated output as a new verified revision only after target validation and semantic checks.
Package and checkpoint cleanup **MUST** occur only after replacement durability, retention-horizon, and reachability proofs succeed.
Portable package generation **MUST** be deterministic at the logical object level even when ZIP byte layout, timestamps, or compression differ.
File and asset parsing **MUST** enforce bounded entry counts, sizes, expansion ratios, paths, nesting, and decoder work before expensive allocation.
Credentials, provider SDK objects, signed URLs, file handles, object URLs, decoded resources, and cache state **MUST NOT** enter canonical document or portable package semantics.
Storage telemetry **MUST** expose bounded save, checkpoint, upload, conflict, recovery, integrity, and garbage-collection hooks without content, identities, or locators.
A shared presentation **MUST** have exactly one durable canonical accepted-operation stream per document epoch.
The collaboration authority **MUST** assign a contiguous monotonic sequence to each accepted transaction within an epoch.
